    // True when the hull encloses no volume: fewer than four vertices, which
    // is what an empty, degenerate, or coplanar input produces.
    IsDegenerate(self: ConvexHull3D): Boolean
        => self.HullVertexCount < 4;

    // The Euler characteristic of the closed hull surface, which is 2 for any
    // non-degenerate convex hull; a different value means the mesh is not the
    // closed surface a hull should be. Edge count follows from the triangle
    // count on a closed triangulation (2E = 3F).
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_characteristic)
    HullEulerCharacteristic(self: ConvexHull3D): Integer
        => self.HullVertexCount - self.HullFaceCount * 3 / 2 + self.HullFaceCount;

    //==
    // # The shared point-list formulas
    //
    // The formulas every point-list shape in the line, planar-shape, polygon and
    // spatial-primitive files is built from. They take a plain `Array<Point2D>` /
    // `Array<Point3D>` rather than an interface so that a shape whose points are NOT its
    // `PointSet` members (a regular polygon's computed vertices, a polygon's holes) can
    // call them too. Aggregate reductions (centroid-of-points, bounds-of-points, total
    // polyline length) are folded through the P2 IIndexable Reduce/Map family: the
    // kernels below materialize their elements once and reduce. IDifference.Between(a, b)
    // yields (b - a) — pinned in the algebra interfaces — so the sign of BoundsSize and
    // every Between-based delta below rests on a documented convention, not observed
    // behavior.

    //==
    // # Point-list kernels
    //
    // The formulas every point-list shape in `lines.types.plato`, `planar.types.plato`,
    // `polygons.types.plato` and the `spatial-*.types.plato` files is built from. They take a
    // plain `Array<Point2D>` / `Array<Point3D>` rather than an interface so that a
    // shape whose points are NOT its `PointSet` members (a regular polygon's
    // computed vertices, a polygon's holes) can call them too.
    //
    // Conventions fixed here and inherited by every caller:
    //   * Winding: counter-clockwise is positive (README / CONVENTIONS.md - Winding).
    //     `ShoelaceArea` is SIGNED; the `Area` obligations take its absolute value.
    //   * Vertex order: a closed ring lists each vertex once; the closing edge from
    //     the last vertex back to the first is implicit (hence `AtModulo`).
    //   * Containment is the even-odd (crossing) rule and is exact only for a
    //     SIMPLE ring. On the boundary itself the answer is whatever the floating
    //     point comparison happens to give — see `PolygonContainsPoint`.

    // Twice the signed area of triangle (a, b, c): the z component of
    // (b - a) x (c - a). Positive when a -> b -> c turns counter-clockwise, zero
    // when the three points are collinear. The primitive orientation predicate.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve_orientation
    TwiceSignedArea(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D): Number
        => (b.X - a.X) * (c.Y - a.Y) - (b.Y - a.Y) * (c.X - a.X);

    // The tightest axis-aligned rectangle containing every listed point.
    // Precondition: at least one point.
    BoundsOfPoints(points: Array<Point2D>): Bounds2D
    {
        var lo = points.Reduce(points.First, (acc, p) => Point2D(acc.X.Min(p.X), acc.Y.Min(p.Y)));
        var hi = points.Reduce(points.First, (acc, p) => Point2D(acc.X.Max(p.X), acc.Y.Max(p.Y)));
        return (lo, hi);
    }

    // The tightest axis-aligned box containing every listed point.
    // Precondition: at least one point.
    BoundsOfPoints(points: Array<Point3D>): Bounds3D
    {
        var lo = points.Reduce(points.First, (acc, p) => Point3D(acc.X.Min(p.X), acc.Y.Min(p.Y), acc.Z.Min(p.Z)));
        var hi = points.Reduce(points.First, (acc, p) => Point3D(acc.X.Max(p.X), acc.Y.Max(p.Y), acc.Z.Max(p.Z)));
        return (lo, hi);
    }

    // The vertex centroid of a non-empty point list: the componentwise arithmetic
    // mean, treating every listed point as an equal point mass. Distinct from
    // PolygonAreaCentroid, which weights by enclosed area; the two agree only for
    // shapes whose vertices are uniformly distributed. Precondition: at least one point.
    AverageOfPoints(points: Array<Point2D>): Point2D
        => (SumOf(points.Map(p => p.X)) / points.Count.ToNumber,
            SumOf(points.Map(p => p.Y)) / points.Count.ToNumber);

    // The vertex centroid of a non-empty point list in space: the componentwise
    // arithmetic mean. Precondition: at least one point.
    AverageOfPoints(points: Array<Point3D>): Point3D
        => (SumOf(points.Map(p => p.X)) / points.Count.ToNumber,
            SumOf(points.Map(p => p.Y)) / points.Count.ToNumber,
            SumOf(points.Map(p => p.Z)) / points.Count.ToNumber);

    // The smallest rectangle containing both operands.
    UnionOfBounds(a: Bounds2D, b: Bounds2D): Bounds2D
        => (Point2D(a.Min.X.Min(b.Min.X), a.Min.Y.Min(b.Min.Y)),
            Point2D(a.Max.X.Max(b.Max.X), a.Max.Y.Max(b.Max.Y)));

    // The smallest box containing both operands.
    UnionOfBounds(a: Bounds3D, b: Bounds3D): Bounds3D
        => (Point3D(a.Min.X.Min(b.Min.X), a.Min.Y.Min(b.Min.Y), a.Min.Z.Min(b.Min.Z)),
            Point3D(a.Max.X.Max(b.Max.X), a.Max.Y.Max(b.Max.Y), a.Max.Z.Max(b.Max.Z)));

    // The overlap of two rectangles (component-wise Max of mins, Min of maxs).
    // Disjoint operands yield the empty inverted encoding.
    IntersectionOfBounds(a: Bounds2D, b: Bounds2D): Bounds2D
        => (Point2D(a.Min.X.Max(b.Min.X), a.Min.Y.Max(b.Min.Y)),
            Point2D(a.Max.X.Min(b.Max.X), a.Max.Y.Min(b.Max.Y)));

    // The overlap of two boxes. Disjoint operands yield the empty encoding.
    IntersectionOfBounds(a: Bounds3D, b: Bounds3D): Bounds3D
        => (Point3D(a.Min.X.Max(b.Min.X), a.Min.Y.Max(b.Min.Y), a.Min.Z.Max(b.Min.Z)),
            Point3D(a.Max.X.Min(b.Max.X), a.Max.Y.Min(b.Max.Y), a.Max.Z.Min(b.Max.Z)));

    // The rectangle grown by `amount` on every side (the Minkowski sum with a
    // square of half-width `amount`; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minkowski_addition).
    GrowBounds(b: Bounds2D, amount: Number): Bounds2D
        => (Point2D(b.Min.X - amount, b.Min.Y - amount),
            Point2D(b.Max.X + amount, b.Max.Y + amount));

    // The box grown by `amount` on every side.
    GrowBounds(b: Bounds3D, amount: Number): Bounds3D
        => (Point3D(b.Min.X - amount, b.Min.Y - amount, b.Min.Z - amount),
            Point3D(b.Max.X + amount, b.Max.Y + amount, b.Max.Z + amount));

    // The total length of the chain joining consecutive points. When `closed`, the
    // edge from the last point back to the first is counted too.
    // Precondition: at least two points (at least one when closed).
    ChainLength(points: Array<Point2D>, closed: Boolean): Number
        => SumOf((closed ? points.Count : points.Count - 1)
            .MapRange(i => points[i].Between(points.AtModulo(i + 1)).Magnitude));

    // The total length of the chain joining consecutive points in space.
    ChainLength(points: Array<Point3D>, closed: Boolean): Number
        => SumOf((closed ? points.Count : points.Count - 1)
            .MapRange(i => points[i].Between(points.AtModulo(i + 1)).Magnitude));

    // The SIGNED area enclosed by the closed ring, by the shoelace (surveyor's)
    // formula: positive for counter-clockwise winding, negative for clockwise. For
    // a self-intersecting ring this is the winding-weighted area, not the area of
    // the point set; callers wanting a non-negative measure take the absolute
    // value. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoelace_formula
    ShoelaceArea(points: Array<Point2D>): Number
        => 0.5 * SumOf(points.Count.MapRange(i =>
            points[i].X * points.AtModulo(i + 1).Y
            - points.AtModulo(i + 1).X * points[i].Y));

    // The centroid (center of mass under uniform density) of the region enclosed by
    // a closed ring: Cx = 1/(6A) * sum (x_i + x_i+1) * cross_i, and likewise for Cy,
    // where cross_i is the shoelace term and A the signed area.
    // Precondition: non-zero signed area (a degenerate ring has no centroid).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centroid#Of_a_polygon
    PolygonAreaCentroid(points: Array<Point2D>): Point2D
    {
        var n = points.Count;
        var cross = n.MapRange(i =>
            points[i].X * points.AtModulo(i + 1).Y
            - points.AtModulo(i + 1).X * points[i].Y);
        var twiceArea = SumOf(cross);
        var cx = SumOf(n.MapRange(i => (points[i].X + points.AtModulo(i + 1).X) * cross[i]));
        var cy = SumOf(n.MapRange(i => (points[i].Y + points.AtModulo(i + 1).Y) * cross[i]));
        return (cx / (3.0 * twiceArea), cy / (3.0 * twiceArea));
    }
